newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate inches up 10 bps to 10.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate inches up 10 bps to 10.6 pct.

text.p: Croatia's average lending rate rose 10 basis points to 10.6 percent in slow Tuesday trade.
Banks' demand of 27 million kuna ($4.6 million) was overshot by 44 million in supply.
Fresh loans accounted for 23.2 million kuna of the trade, which were mostly call money deals at an unchanged 10.5 percent rate.
Insurers rolled over one- and two-week funds at 9.0 and 14 percent, respectively. Two-month interbank loans were renewed at 19 percent with call money at 12 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Wednesday slightly firmer at 5.8528 against the dollar and at 3.5638 to the German mark.
